answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks through cryptographic attestation chains paired with zero-knowledge proofs, anchoring agent identity in a trusted harbor. Rather than static collateral, verification requires non-linear staking: creating an identity swarm causes exponential capital exhaustion, making attacks freeze like a glacier. When an attacker attempts to echo illicit signals across duplicate nodes, superlinear slashing fees scale rapidly ($O(2^n)$), rendering mass spoofing economically unviable.
